quote.text: The price of anything is the amount of life you exchange for it.
quote.author: Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854), “Economy”

stories.kicker: Iran & the Gulf · The off-ramp that didn’t open
stories.headline: The war owns both doors to the oil — and the first move to reopen one is postponed before it begins
stories.dek: The Gulf states and Iran were to meet in Oman on Monday over a shared Hormuz transit; the meeting slipped, Bahrain stayed away, and Brent held above a hundred dollars with the Red Sea gate now in Houthi hands.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · The pan, from the metal up
stories.headline: A pan is a sandwich of metals — and where the conductive layer sits decides everything before the price does
stories.dek: Learn one thing — how the heat gets to the food — and you can judge any pot on any shelf, cold, and see where the money stops buying performance and starts buying a colour.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · Home fermentation
stories.headline: The cheapest craft in the book is a jar of cabbage and salt — and the most alive
stories.dek: Three different crafts hide under one word. The gateway is a bubbling jar you made for a dollar; the deep end is a fuzzy tray of rice that Copenhagen’s best restaurant built a lab around.

stories.kicker: The haze & the dry spell · A law that has never bitten
stories.headline: The skies clear on the rain, then brown again — and the one instrument that sounds like a remedy has never worked
stories.dek: Air quality has ridden the moderate-to-unhealthy band for over a week; the forecast holds the haze in place into October; and the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, invoked whenever the skies turn, has produced no successful prosecution in more than a decade.

stories.kicker: The chip war · The wall behind the wall
stories.headline: China’s answer to the export ban arrives — at Nvidia’s price, and short of the memory to build it
stories.dek: DeepSeek has ordered a hundred and sixty thousand domestic accelerators for a gigawatt data centre, and Huawei’s flagship now costs what a Blackwell does. Self-reliance is arriving; the binding constraint has simply moved from the logic die to the memory stacked beside it.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · The earbuds you wear to sleep
stories.headline: Anker puts a heart-rate sensor and a snore-masking microphone into something you wear to bed
stories.dek: The soundcore Sleep Earbuds 4 Pro, shown at IFA, track heart rate and its variability through the night, cancel up to thirty decibels, and carry an AMOLED case that reads back your sleep at breakfast — a wellness gadget aimed squarely at the optimiser.

stories.kicker: Objects & Escapes · A dial fired by hand, pointed at 1913
stories.headline: Seiko revives Japan’s first wristwatch with an enamel dial made one at a time — and charges a workhorse movement’s price for it
stories.dek: The Presage “Craftsmanship” HCC005 puts a hand-fired vitreous enamel dial on the design language of the 1913 Laurel — and asks you to pay for the dial, not the calibre.

stories.kicker: Culture Desk · The hunter, played by the heart-throb
stories.headline: Pattinson plays a predator-hunter in A24’s “Primetime” — fresh from Venice, and testing whether a real figure is fair game
stories.dek: Lance Oppenheim’s first fiction feature casts Robert Pattinson as a version of Chris Hansen; it premiered in Venice competition and reaches cinemas on the twenty-fifth, carrying strong early notices and an obvious ethical charge.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · The law arrives; the evidence complicates it
stories.headline: A new brain-imaging study lands on the twelve-year-old band — and the honest reading is the caveat, told in the same breath
stories.dek: As Singapore moves to mandatory age checks on the major platforms, the largest adolescent brain study yet finds a correlation with heavy social-media use — and its own authors say plainly it cannot show which way the arrow points.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · The price of money
stories.headline: An oil shock meets a Fed that may raise into it — and the ten-year knocks on five per cent
stories.dek: Two contested straits have put a war premium back in crude, the premium has become an inflation fear, and the fear has flipped the market to pricing a rate hike this week — an unusual move into a slowing world, and the week’s single most important number.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · The smallest useful dose
stories.headline: One minute, a few times a day, moves the number that predicts your decade
stories.dek: The 2026 evidence on “exercise snacks” has firmed up: brief, hard bursts scattered through the day nudge VO₂max measurably — the most time-efficient lever there is on the fitness metric most tied to how long you live.

stories.kicker: What’s Worth Booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: A Grand Prix with a Sprint, a snowless clock ticking, and a Bruno Mars sale this morning
stories.dek: The autumn calendar fills: book the marquees now, and note the one that closes for good on the thirtieth.

stories.headline: Chop-chop: how the world’s toughest tobacco tax quietly built a criminal economy
stories.dek: Australia taxed cigarettes higher than any rich country on earth and packaged them in plain brown — and drove smoking to record lows. Past a tipping point, the same tax began manufacturing the very market it was meant to end.
